ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has two panels. The left panel, titled All Animals, plots annual sightings from 2005 to 2008 for cougars, deer, chipmunk, skunk, and raccoon. The deer line declines noticeably across the years, from high sightings in 2005 to much lower sightings by 2008. Raccoons remain high with only a moderate late decrease, chipmunks fluctuate, and skunks stay low with small changes. The right panel, titled Cougars, shows cougar sightings dropping steadily and sharply from about 6 in 2005 to 0 in 2008. Reasoning: To infer the most probable primary prey, compare prey population trends with the cougar decline. The species whose decline most plausibly supports the cougar population decrease is deer, because deer sightings drop markedly over the same 2005–2008 interval while the other non-cougar species do not match the cougar decrease as well.

raw_record.question_text: What species is the most probable primary prey for the cougar population according to the figure?

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: it has a separate cougar sightings panel showing a steady drop across 2005–2008, and an all-animals panel with labeled lines for deer, raccoon, chipmunk, skunk, and cougars. Compare each non-cougar species trend with the cougar decline. Deer drops markedly over the same interval, whereas the other animal lines do not match the cougar decrease as well. Apply the predator-prey trend rule: the primary prey is the species whose population trend most plausibly supports the cougar population trend. Conclude that the most probable primary prey is deer.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct visual-correlation route: use the species trend lines in the figure and identify which potential prey population changes most consistently with the cougar trend, rather than relying on outside cougar diet facts alone.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the right panel to see cougar sightings decline from about 6 in 2005 to 0 in 2008. Read the left panel legend and trend lines for all animals: deer sightings decline strongly over the same years, while raccoon remains high and only slightly declines, chipmunk is relatively stable after 2006, and skunk remains low/slightly variable.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to identify the target: name the species that is the most probable primary prey for the cougar population according to the figure.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the ecological bridge that a predator population is most likely to track the availability of its primary prey; the prey whose abundance declines in parallel with cougar sightings is the most probable primary prey.
